title: Orgasm dynamic response model
description: A bounded computational model of sexual climax as a composite dynamical response built from neural excitation, autonomic activation, sensory/rhythmic feedback, and inhibitory control. This record is a hypothesis/model specification, not a claim that orgasm has a universal resonant frequency.
definitions: O(t) = bounded model output in [0,1] representing modeled climax intensity.
assumptions: All component terms are normalized model variables rather than direct clinical measurements.
The frequency variable f is a simulation parameter and is not asserted to be a biological law.
The model describes system dynamics abstractly and does not infer an individual's sexual state.
A numerical peak in O(t) is a model event, not evidence of a measured orgasm.
mechanism: The model combines excitation, autonomic activation, sensory feedback and inhibition into a single state variable, then maps that state through a sigmoid threshold function. The resonance term is included as a generic dynamical-system component so different frequencies can be compared reproducibly.
falsification_conditions: The model fails its declared software tests for bounded output O(t) in [0,1].
A defined empirical dataset, if later supplied, systematically contradicts the model predictions under preregistered comparison rules.
The resonance component adds no reproducible explanatory value relative to a declared null model.
confusion_guard: Do not interpret the simulated O(t) value as a physiological measurement, diagnosis, or universal frequency of orgasm. Simulation is not measurement.
